scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

Long-term responsibilities like parenting can shape your outlook in several ways: 1. **Develops resilience and adaptability**: Managing the needs of your children requires flexibility and adaptability. You learn to navigate unexpected situations, prioritize tasks, and adjust to changing circumstances. These skills help you develop resilience, which can benefit you in various areas of life. 2. **Enhances time management and organization**: Coordinating schedules, meal planning, and keeping track of details can help you develop strong time management and organizational skills. These skills are transferable to other areas of life, such as work, personal projects, or even volunteering. 3. **Fosters empathy and compassion**: Caring for children teaches you to be more empathetic and understanding. You learn to put yourself in their shoes and consider their needs, which can broaden your perspective and help you become a more compassionate person. 4. **Encourages selflessness and prioritization**: As a mother, you often put the needs of your children before your own. This selfless attitude can help you develop a sense of purpose and prioritize what's truly important in life. 5. **Shapes your values and priorities**: Parenting influences your values and priorities, helping you focus on what truly matters. You may find that your priorities shift from personal goals to family-oriented goals, which can lead to a more fulfilling life. 6. **Develops problem-solving skills**: Managing the challenges of parenting requires creative problem-solving. You learn to think critically, find solutions, and make decisions under pressure. 7. **Enhances emotional intelligence**: Parenting helps you develop emotional intelligence by teaching you to recognize, understand, and manage your emotions. This skill is essential for building strong relationships and navigating complex social situations. 8. **Provides a sense of purpose and fulfillment**: Raising children can give you a sense of purpose and fulfillment, as you watch them grow and develop. This can lead to a more positive outlook on life and a greater sense of satisfaction. While the responsibilities of parenting can be challenging, they also offer numerous opportunities for growth and development. By embracing these experiences, you can cultivate a more resilient, adaptable, and compassionate outlook on life. How do you find that your experiences as a mother have shaped your outlook on life?
